title: Pause, inspect, and step with the Node.js debugger

location.start: Begin at “Debugger” and read the “Interactive mode” example through “Watchers”.
location.stop: Stop after the Interactive mode and Watchers sections. Do not use setBreakpoint, conditional breakpoints, remote debugging, probe mode, or V8 inspector integration.
location.note:
Do: Create `debug-search.js` with these exact lines: `const title = "  Review Functions  ";` `const query = "review";` `const normalizedTitle = title.trim().toLowerCase();` `const normalizedQuery = query.trim().toLowerCase();` `debugger;` `const matches = normalizedTitle === normalizedQuery;` `console.log(matches);`. Run `node inspect debug-search.js`; at the first pause type `cont`; at the `debugger;` pause add `watch("normalizedTitle")` and `watch("normalizedQuery")`, use `repl` to read either value, then leave the REPL with Ctrl+C. Type `next` twice so the comparison executes, enter `repl` again, and read `matches`. Record that equality asks whether the full strings match, whereas the intended substring rule needs `normalizedTitle.includes(normalizedQuery)`. Repair the comparison, rerun, and remove the `debugger;` statement after recording the result.

Finished when: You can use a deliberate `debugger;` statement, `cont`, `watch()`, `repl`, and `next` to observe both operands and the false result, explain the wrong comparison, and verify the repaired substring match.

title: Publish an existing local project safely

location.start: Begin with the warning about sensitive information.
location.stop: Stop after the first successful push and repository refresh.
location.note:
Do: Read the warning and the command-line steps for adding locally hosted code through the first push. Before `git add .`, copy the supplied `.gitignore`, replace `data/items.json` with `[]` or a sanitized sample, and run `git status --short`. After staging, run `git status --short` again and inspect every listed path. If a secret, personal record, log, or unrelated file is staged, do not commit: run `git rm --cached -- <path>` to keep it locally, correct the ignore/data choice, and inspect again. At the first push, use Git Credential Manager or the browser sign-in for the verified free GitHub account from Setup; never paste a credential into source or README.

Finished when: You can show the final `git status --short` review and a public or shareable repository containing intended source, tests, package metadata, README, and sanitized sample data—but no secret or private learner data.

Access: A free verified GitHub account is required to publish. If setup already verified one, no new account is needed.

Next: Run the final acceptance checklist, submit proof, and complete the final reflection.
